riskDescription.context: As of July 22, 2026, Integration Testing, UAT, and Penetration Test are all at 0% progress (ART - WSR). Data Hub Integration is 95% complete but 22 days past its revised date of June 30 (ART - WSR). Go Live is scheduled for September 2, 2026, 42 days away (ART - Work Assignment, ART - WSR). UAT Signoff is needed by August 14 (23 days away) and Penetration Test by August 25 (34 days away) (ART - WSR).
riskDescription.condition: The remaining testing phases may not complete in the available time, especially if Data Hub Integration delays persist or if testing uncovers issues requiring rework.
riskDescription.consequence: Go Live on September 2 may be delayed, affecting the client relationship and the ability to onboard 2,500+ producers as planned.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Rebaseline impacted scope with the customer, prioritize critical-path functionality, and adjust sprint priorities to protect the September 2 Production rollout.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon any testing phase delay beyond August 25, immediately re-baseline the go-live plan, identify the earliest available release window, and escalate to the project board within 48 hours.
risks.reasoning: Three major testing phases are at 0% with only 42 days to Go Live, and a key dependency (DH Integration) is incomplete and overdue. The compressed timeline leaves little room for issue remediation. Evidence is corroborated across multiple sections of the WSR.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Conduct daily collaboration with DH and business teams to validate data mappings, and rebaseline the impacted scope if design changes are required.

risks.reasoning: The dependency is overdue by 22 days and an open risk explicitly warns of potential design rework. Integration Testing cannot proceed without stable DH integration, and the timeline is already compressed.

riskDescription.context: As of June 18, 2026, backend code coverage is 57% (ART - WSR), below the typical 80% target. There are 190 code smells in progress, including 2 Critical and 80 Major (ART - WSR). The WSR notes that code quality issues are a challenge impacting the October 15 release target, and that design adherence and unit testing implementation continue to be key areas for improvement (ART - WSR). Functional test failure rate is 15% (11 of 71 test cases failed) (ART - WSR).
riskDescription.condition: The backend code coverage gap and unresolved code smells may allow defects to remain undetected until Integration Testing or UAT.
riskDescription.consequence: Defects may surface late in testing, requiring rework and delaying UAT or Go Live, or defects may reach production, weakening client confidence.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Increase manual code review frequency with senior developers, prioritize resolution of 2 Critical and 80 Major code smells, and target 80% backend code coverage by August 10.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: If code quality issues surface during Integration Testing, schedule additional review sessions with senior developers, seek client input on priorities, and implement defect triage to protect the go-live date.
risks.reasoning: Code coverage is measurably below standard (57% vs 80%), and the WSR explicitly calls out code quality as a challenge impacting release. The 15% functional test failure rate and 190 code smells corroborate the quality gap. Testing phases ahead may uncover issues requiring rework.

riskDescription.context: The WSR notes that end-to-end workflow and impacted-path validation needs strengthening to reduce regression leakage (ART - WSR). Integration Testing is at 0% progress (ART - WSR). There are 190 code smells in progress, including 2 Critical and 80 Major (ART - WSR).
riskDescription.condition: Regression testing practices may remain insufficient, and Integration Testing may not catch all regression issues before UAT.
riskDescription.consequence: Regression defects may reach UAT or production, requiring emergency fixes and potentially delaying Go Live or causing post-production issues.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Strengthen end-to-end workflow validation by expanding regression test coverage, executing regression pipelines on ACPT, and validating impacted paths before UAT.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon detection of regression leakage in UAT, activate defect triage with senior developers, prioritize critical-path fixes, and communicate revised timelines to stakeholders within 24 hours.
risks.reasoning: The WSR explicitly identifies regression leakage as a concern and calls for strengthening validation practices. Integration Testing has not started, so the effectiveness of regression prevention is unproven. The code smell backlog increases the risk of regression.

riskDescription.context: The WSR documents multiple open risks related to AAVA agent performance: Single LLM may underperform on specific tasks (March 16 risk); inadequate agent hardening may cause inconsistent behavior in production (March 16 risk); limited training datasets may delay agent maturity (March 16 risk); agent dependency on external tools may result in execution failures (March 16 risk); poor coordination between multiple agents may cause workflow delays (March 16 risk) (ART - WSR). risks.reasoning: Five open risks explicitly document agent performance concerns, and agent efficiency metrics show significant manual effort still required. The risks are dated March 2026 and remain open. Production use of agents introduces uncertainty about behavior under load.

riskDescription.context: Go Live is scheduled for September 2, 2026 (ART - Work Assignment, ART - WSR). The portal is intended to onboard producers across all lines of business. Testing phases are compressed with multiple quality and security risks identified across R-001, R-006, R-007, and R-008.
riskDescription.condition: If Go Live proceeds on September 2 with incomplete testing or unresolved quality issues, the mass producer onboarding may encounter functional, performance, or security issues.
riskDescription.consequence: Producer onboarding may fail or be rolled back, causing client dissatisfaction, reputational damage, and potential commercial penalties or disputes.

risks.mitigationPreventiveAction: Rebaseline impacted scope with the customer, prioritize critical-path functionality, agree on phased delivery if required, and validate end-to-end registration process before mass onboarding.
risks.contingencyCorrectiveAction: Upon detection of functional, performance, or security issues during mass onboarding, immediately activate rollback procedures, communicate the issue to program leadership within 1 hour, and implement phased onboarding as backup.
risks.reasoning: This risk cascades from R-001, R-006, R-007, and R-008. Multiple quality and testing risks threaten release readiness. Mass onboarding amplifies the impact of any production issue. The compressed timeline increases the likelihood of issues reaching production.
